text:
matt: Hey team, support got an urgent escalation from Acme — p99 on their /v1/generate route jumped from ~220ms to 2.8s around 16:12 UTC. Customer sees timeouts and retries. They say degradation started after yesterday's model rollout.

lina: copying logs from the dedicated pool that serves them — hitting a lot of GPU memory allocation slow paths and occasional OOMs, but what’s odd is throughput drops before full OOM. Looks like fragmentation + KV cache growth.

matt: snippet from their app logs they attached:
```
2026-03-16T16:11:59Z ERROR rpc: request timeout (deadline exceeded) route=/v1/generate user=acct_XXX
2026-03-16T16:12:02Z WARN runtime: alloc failed, falling back to slow allocator
2026-03-16T16:12:04Z ERROR gpu: out of memory while allocating 64MB for kv_cache
```

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-20260316-1456 (severity: high) — assigned to eng-runtime oncall.

tara: Can you paste the Prometheus queries for GPU mem and KV cache sizes? I want to see trends vs request concurrency.

lina: PromQLs below — ran these over the affected cluster window:
```
avg_over_time(gpu_memory_used_bytes{pool="dedicated-acme"}[1h])
max_over_time(kv_cache_bytes{pool="dedicated-acme"}[30m])
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le))
```
The plots show kv_cache_bytes steady grow per worker; p95 rises as kv grows, then p99 spikes when allocations hit slow paths.

matt: customer says they’re using a long-chat model with large context and lots of small concurrent sessions — likely very high KV retention per connection. Could be a leak or our retention policy not triggering.

kyle: Two things to triage quickly: 1) confirm whether KV eviction is per-shard or global (we have a known case where per-connection retention accumulates when sessions reattach), 2) check allocator behavior — jemalloc stats show large fragmentation in older kernels.

tara: Agreed. Short-term mitigations for customer: a) reduce per-connection KV retention (config flag: `--kv-max-bytes-per-session=8MB`), b) lower batching window to reduce concurrent peak memory, c) scale up pool by +1 GPU while we investigate. Any objections?

lina: No objections. I'll apply kv limit and lower batching to 10ms on their pool for a quick canary. Please prepare a rollback plan.

matt: Customer accepted temporary scale-up and config change. Applying now.

kyle: For root cause, I want the following repro artifacts: a) heap profile (nvprof/alloc traces) from a worker during a spike, b) KV cache per-session histogram, c) sequence length distribution and concurrency map. Command to fetch alloc profile:
```bash
kubectl exec -it worker-abc -- curl -s localhost:9100/debug/alloc?format=jemalloc > alloc.json
```
Also, perf note: set env `JEMALLOC_CONF=\"lg_chunk:22,dirty_decay_ms:60000\"` for a canary to reduce fragmentation.

lina: I'll collect profiles now and attach. If jemalloc tweak helps, we can roll as a platform flag.

tara: Also check whether our KV cache eviction is disabled for model variant v2.3 — I recall a recent change to preserve conversation state for reconnects. That could cause kv growth for long-running sessions.

matt: Repro steps for support ticket (so they can test with loadgen):
1) start 200 concurrent sessions with average seq_len=2048 and intermittent reconnects
2) maintain 3 requests/sec per session for 15 minutes
3) watch `kv_cache_bytes` + `gpu_memory_used_bytes` and p99 latency

lina: Uploading alloc profile and per-session kv histogram to the incident. Preliminary look: many sessions show KV retention ~12-20MB each, we have ~120 active sessions per worker => ~2.4GB just KV. Combined with model activations and fragmentation, that pushes allocation slow paths.

kyle: Plan: short term = config limits + jemalloc canary + scale up. Medium = enforce per-session hard cap + add periodic KV compaction/eviction policy, plus a rollout to fix variant v2.3 behavior. Long term = telemetry alert that triggers when kv_cache_bytes / gpu_total_bytes > 0.6 and p95 > 500ms.

oncall-bot: Action assigned: lina -> apply canary (+kv limit), kyle -> prepare jemalloc rollout, tara -> verify model variant config, matt -> coordinate with customer and update support ticket.

matt: I'll update the customer in 30 mins with mitigations and ETA for root-cause fix. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
